items.title: Show HN: A calendar tracker for OpenAI's 28-day Codex reset challenge
items.contentSnippet:
OpenAI recently announced a 28-day reset challenge: each day, either a "clear improvement" or a usage reset.
I built this calendar to track the challenge. It updates throughout the day as updates become available.
The site also has every reset since April 2025 backfilled, along with a "percent on time" chart similar to airline flights.
This is part of a new project called ResetAlerts, which sends alerts about the latest Codex resets. Open to any thoughts, feedback, or features you want to see.

items.title: Show HN: Tilefinch – a from-scratch* web browser for the PSP (333Mhz, 64MB RAM)
items.contentSnippet:
I picked up my PSP for the first time in about a decade and wanted to find out three things: how far the hardware could be pushed, how much of the modern web fits on it, and what today’s coding agents can do. A web browser tests all three.
Tilefinch runs entirely on a PSP-3000: networking, HTML, CSS, JavaScript, layout and rendering, over Wi-Fi, with no proxy or companion computer. The style, layout, paint, media and UI layers are new C code and a patched QuickJS runs the JavaScript.

items.title: Show HN: SupplyVision – I made meta-search for independent fashion retailers
items.contentSnippet:
I made a search engine to find fashion deals across hundreds of independent fashion retailers.
Fun technical stuff:
- It doesn't do any webpage parsing to fill the index, instead relying on the UCP protocol.
- It uses a complex deterministic engine that merges listings based on very messy and unreliable data from retailers (no, Jev can't do that).
- It parses shipping rules and compares prices after delivery and duties.

items.title: Show HN: I added optional chaining to CPython
items.contentSnippet:
I forked CPython to experiment with adding optional chaining (?.) directly to the language.
For example:
name = response?.customer?.name.lower()
If response or customer is None, the expression short-circuits and evaluates to None. This isn't a library or a transpiler change, but a direct CPython modification.
A bit about the build: I used AI extensively for this experiment. Part of my motivation was to see how far I can get the modification in an unfamiliar codebase like CPython.

items.title: Show HN: How good is your Rust? Free quiz, every code answer checked by rustc
items.contentSnippet:
I run rustcoach, an AI-guided Rust course. This is the free, no-signup part of it: a 30-question test across core Rust, async/Tokio, macros, concurrency/atomics and the type system, plus a 20-question test for each of those areas if you want to dig depper (also free, no registration). At the end you get a level, a per-area breakdown and a suggestion of what to learn next.
